fields.meta_title: Referral Landing Page Examples You Can Build | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See four referral landing page examples, then build one that names the referrer, holds each reward until it counts, and saves every referral.
fields.h1: Build a Referral Landing Page That Knows Who Sent Each Friend
fields.hero_description: Build a referral landing page that greets each friend by the referrer's name and saves every referral to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Sits Between a Shared Link and a Reward
fields.features_subheading: A referral landing page serves the customer who shares a link and the friend who opens it. These six parts keep both straight.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the program, get the page

Write down the reward, who earns it, and when a referral counts. Emergent builds the invite page and the table behind it from that prompt, then changes any part when you ask again.
fields.feature_2:
The referrer's name on every invite

Each friend lands on a page that says who sent them, such as Priya Raman invited you. The name comes from the link the friend opened, so no one types a code to credit the referrer.
fields.feature_3:
One link and one code per customer

Every referrer gets a personal link to share and a short code to text or read aloud. Both point to the same person, so a friend using either one is credited to the right referrer.
fields.feature_4:
Rewards that wait for a condition

Pick the moment a referral pays out, such as a first finished visit or a month as a customer. Until then the reward shows as Pending, and it moves to Earned once that moment comes.
fields.feature_5:
Every referral saved as a row you own

Each referral saves to a database you own with the referrer, the friend, the date, and the reward status. A live dashboard counts referrals per person and shows who shares the most.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, your code when needed

Run the program on your own domain; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when a developer wants to extend it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Her friend's page opens on Priya's name

Tallyroot sells invoicing software to freelancers. When Priya Raman shares her link, the page her friend opens reads Priya Raman invited you, right above the signup form. Okon Hale signed up there. His row saved with Priya as the referrer, and her count moved to 4 friends joined.
fields.tab_content_2:
A $40 credit waits for the first finished visit

Brightmoss Lawn Care pays its referrers in service credit, $40 for each new customer they send. Delphine Arceneaux referred her neighbor Gus Malloy, and her credit sat at Pending until his first mowing visit was marked done. The crew lead closed that visit, and the credit moved to Earned.
fields.tab_content_3:
Imani books a free ride on Ravi's link

Every Corvane Cycle member can give away one free first ride. Imani Brooks opened Ravi Thakkar's link and picked the Saturday 9:00 ride from the open classes, which left 4 bikes. Her booking saved with Ravi's name on it, and the studio can see which members bring in new riders.
fields.tab_content_4:
Noor is 2 friends from a free month

Pinegate Coffee ships beans on subscription, and every subscriber has a status page with a personal link and a running count. Noor Haddad's page shows 3 friends joined and her free bag unlocked. Two more friends take her to 5 and a free month of coffee.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Referral Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow seven steps to create a referral landing page that credits the right referrer and releases each reward once it counts.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose the reward each side gets
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide the moment a referral counts
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Lead the friend's page with a name
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what the reward needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the referrer earns and what the friend gets, such as a $40 credit for one and a free first visit for the other. Give both sides something: the friend gets a reason to act, and the referrer gets a line to say when sharing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the one event that moves a reward from Pending to Earned, such as a signup or a first finished visit. Then state it on the page in one plain sentence. A referrer who knows the rule will not wonder why a reward has not arrived.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the referrer's name in the first line of the friend's page, and the friend's reward right under it. A name the friend knows belongs above your logo and above any product claim on the page.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the form to the fields you need to credit the referral and deliver the reward, such as a name and an email. Ask for a delivery address or a class time on the next screen, after the friend has signed up.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the program in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the reward, the counting rule, the form fields, and the words for Pending and Earned into one prompt. Emergent builds the pages and the referral table from it. Read the first version as a friend would, then prompt again for changes.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send each customer their own link
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put every customer's personal link in an email they already open, such as a receipt or a monthly update. Add the short code for people who refer in person. Then point regulars to the status page where their count lives.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open your own link in a private browser window and sign up as the friend. Mark the counting event done, then check that the row names the right referrer and that the reward has moved from Pending to Earned.

faq_plan.q: What is a referral landing page?
faq_plan.a: A referral landing page is the page a friend opens from a customer's referral link or code. It names the person who sent the link, states what the friend gets, and asks for a signup or a booking. The signup saves with the referrer's name attached.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a referral landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write one prompt with the reward for each side, the event that makes a referral count, and the fields the friend fills in. Emergent's AI landing page builder turns it into the friend's page, the referrer's status page, and the table that records each referral. Prompt again to change any of them.

faq_plan.q: What should a referral program landing page include?
faq_plan.a: It needs four parts: a reward for each side, the rule for when a referral counts, a short form, and a way to share. Put the friend's reward in the headline and the rule in one plain line under the form. Emergent builds the referral table in a database you own, with a status on every row.

faq_plan.q: What can I learn from referral landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Look at where the referrer's name sits, how the reward is worded, and how many fields the form asks for. Then open each example on a phone and judge it as you would a mobile landing page: one column, with a button a thumb can reach.

faq_plan.q: Should a referral landing page look different for the referrer and the friend?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The friend's page explains the offer and asks for a signup. The referrer's page holds their personal link and their count toward the next reward. Mixing the two puts a share button in front of someone who has not joined yet.

faq_plan.q: How should I phrase the reward on a referral landing page?
faq_plan.a: State the reward and what the friend does to get it in one sentence, such as Your first ride is free when you book a class. Give an exact amount or item instead of a vague discount, and keep the fine print to one line under the button.

faq_plan.q: Should a referral landing page include a short video?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the program needs explaining, such as rewards in tiers. Keep the clip under a minute and place the form beside it, not below it. If the clip is the main event, build a video landing page instead, with the video above everything else.

faq_plan.q: Should a referral landing page use links or codes?
faq_plan.a: Use both, tied to the same referrer. A link suits sharing by text or chat; a code suits referrals made in person. Keep each code short enough to say out loud, such as PRIYA4, and leave out characters that look alike, like O and 0.

faq_plan.q: When should a signup on a referral landing page earn the reward?
faq_plan.a: When the friend does something worth paying for, not when they click. For a service, that can be a first finished visit; for a subscription, the first renewal. Emergent builds that rule from your prompt, and the reward waits at Pending until it is met.

faq_plan.q: How many fields should a referral landing page ask for?
faq_plan.a: Two: a name and an email. Collect anything else after the signup. A referral page asks for less than a lead magnet landing page, which trades a guide for details about the reader. On a page Emergent builds, each signup and the person who sent it sit in a database you own.

plan.angle: Searchers want referral landing page examples, and the AI Overview and image pack answer with galleries and referral-software feature pages that stop at the share button. This page shows four referral pages working after the click: an invite page that greets the friend with the referrer's name, a lawn care credit that waits for the first finished visit, a cycling studio's free ride booked from a member's link, and a referrer status page with reward tiers. Every referral lands as a row in a database the owner keeps. The FAQ covers what a referral program page needs, examples, the friend's page versus the referrer's page, reward wording, codes versus links, and when a referral counts. Referral forms, waitlists and giveaways are siblings and stay out of the headings.
